title: The Mule

full_text:
A mule, fed abundantly on rich oats and barley, grew fat, glossy, and puffed up with boundless conceit. He galloped across the pasture, kicking up his heels and neighing:

"My father was a royal racehorse, swifter than the wind! I have inherited his noble blood, his speed, and his magnificent stature!"

He galloped around the meadow, trying to outrun the wind. But after half a mile, his breath failed, his knees trembled, and he slowed to a plodding, stubborn walk.

Remembering his limitations, he sighed in humility: "Alas, my memory was too short: I remembered my father the racehorse, but I entirely forgot my mother the common donkey!"
moral: Pride in noble ancestry is swiftly humbled when the full heritage is remembered.
